hints: Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 2x^{-3}$ to get $y = x^3 + x^{-2} + c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative with respect to $x$:
$$y = \int \left(3x^2 - 2x^{-3}\right) dx = \frac{3x^3}{3} - \frac{2x^{-2}}{-2} + c = x^3 + x^{-2} + c = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^2} + c$$

Substitute the given coordinates $(-1, 3)$ to determine the constant of integration $c$:
$$3 = (-1)^3 + \frac{1}{(-1)^2} + c = -1 + 1 + c \implies c = 3$$

Write the complete equation of the curve:
$$y = x^3 + x^{-2} + 3 \quad \left(\text{or } y = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^2} + 3\right)$$
